name: Chicken patties with sweet potato & zucchini (קציצות עוף)

source.author: Pasted family-style recipe (Hebrew)
source.notes: 1 kg ground chicken mixed with fried onion, finely grated sweet potato and zucchini, 2 eggs, ~½ cup breadcrumbs, a little ketchup, salt and pepper; rested 1 h in the fridge, spooned (≈2 tbsp each) into a pan and fried over medium heat. Adopted into rotation directly per user request. ASSUMPTIONS (amounts not given — tell me to adjust): ground chicken taken as a standard mixed ground chicken (~8% fat; leaner if it's all breast, fattier if pargit/thigh), 1 medium sweet potato (~150 g), 1 medium zucchini (~200 g), ~1 tbsp oil to fry the onion, ~2 tbsp ketchup, ~1 tsp salt, and ~3 tbsp of frying oil absorbed across the whole batch. Makes ~28-30 patties; analyzed as 8 servings of ~3-4 patties. Estimate.

ingredients.qty: for the pan (~3 tbsp absorbed, assumed)

steps: Fry the chopped onion until soft and golden; cool slightly.
Mix the ground chicken, fried onion, grated sweet potato and zucchini, salt, pepper, ketchup, eggs and breadcrumbs.
Rest the mixture in the fridge about 1 hour.
Spoon about 2 tablespoons per patty into a pan and fry over medium heat until golden on both sides and cooked through.

batch_totals.note: Whole batch (~28–30 patties, 8 servings). Fat is driven by the ground chicken's own fat plus pan-frying oil — the two biggest levers. Grated sweet potato and zucchini add moisture, fibre and vitamin A while stretching the meat.

him.verdict: A solid, family-friendly protein staple: ~25 g protein per ~318 kcal serving, with hidden veg (sweet potato + zucchini) adding moisture, a little fibre and vitamin A. It lands at ~7.9 g protein per 100 kcal — good, but fat (~19 g/serving) is on the higher side from mixed ground chicken plus pan-frying. Using breast mince and baking or spraying instead of shallow-frying would push it to 9.
flags: ~25 g protein / 318 kcal per serving (~7.9 g protein per 100 kcal)
fat ~19 g/serving — ground chicken fat + pan-frying oil
hidden veg: sweet potato + zucchini (vitamin A, moisture, some fibre)
moderate sodium (~474 mg) — salt + ketchup + breadcrumbs
suggested_mods: Use ground chicken breast instead of mixed/pargit — biggest fat cut
Bake on a lined tray at 200 °C ~20 min (flip once) or pan-fry with spray oil instead of shallow oil
Swap breadcrumbs for whole-spelt/whole-wheat breadcrumbs or oats for fibre
Double the zucchini — more volume and moisture for almost no calories

her_preconception.verdict: Good everyday dish for her: lean poultry protein, choline from the eggs, vitamin A (as beta-carotene, the safe form) from sweet potato. Fully cooked — just make sure the centres are cooked through (no pink). Not a big folate or iron source on its own; pair with a green salad.
prenatal_highlights: beta-carotene vitamin A from sweet potato (the pregnancy-safe form)

safety_advisories.note: Ground chicken must be cooked through (74 °C, no pink inside) — check a thick patty.
safety_advisories.swap: lower the heat and cook a little longer if the outside browns before the inside is done

suggested_mods: Serve with a leafy green salad for folate + vitamin C

adopted_note: Adopted 2026-11-08 directly per user request (as written, not optimized). Per serving (~3-4 patties, ~180 g, of 8): ~318 kcal, 25.1 g protein, 12.2 g carb, 18.9 g fat, 1.4 g fibre, ~474 mg sodium. him 7 / her 7. Amounts for sweet potato, zucchini, ketchup, salt and frying oil were assumed — flag actual amounts to tighten. Easy upgrades if wanted later: breast mince, bake/spray-fry, whole-grain crumbs.
cooking_guide: Grate the sweet potato and zucchini finely, then squeeze the zucchini in a towel to remove excess water — otherwise the mix gets too wet and the patties fall apart.
Fry the onion slowly until golden for sweetness, and let it cool before mixing so it doesn't start cooking the raw egg.
Mix just until combined — overworking ground meat makes patties dense and tough.
Don't skip the 1-hour rest in the fridge: the breadcrumbs hydrate and the mix firms up, so the patties hold their shape in the pan.
Wet your hands or the spoon slightly when shaping to stop sticking; flatten each to an even thickness so they cook through evenly.

Fry over MEDIUM heat, not high — the sweet potato and ketchup contain sugar and brown quickly, and you need time for the centre to cook through. Don't crowd the pan; flip once when the underside is golden and releases easily.
Drain briefly on paper towel. Check a thick one in the centre (no pink).
